clue.text: Frigid Brenda's crafty extravagance no longer presents a trendy image of this country

definitions.text: a trendy image of this country

parts.note: frigid means cold, or cool
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen; her craft was the royal yacht Britannia, an extravagance decommissioned in 1997

explanation.surface: A complaint that a chilly royal's costly indulgence has gone, taking a fashionable national image with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, and 'crafty' points to a craft, the royal yacht Britannia, retired in 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the 1990s media slogan for Britain rebranded as fashionable under New Labour.

clue.text: Maybe your member's investing a lot of money in Algerian port

definitions.note: member is, i.e. a member of the body, of which this is an example

indicators.note: investing here means clothing or surrounding, so the port wraps round the money

parts.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A smutty suggestion that your private part is putting cash into a North African harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' looks financial but means enclosing. G, a grand, is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Any organ is a body part, and the clue hints at the rude slang sense of member.

clue.text: Linesman no longer endlessly mucking about

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: larking means mucking about, fooling around

explanation.surface: A football official, out of the game for good, is just messing around with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A linesman here is a writer of lines, a poet; 'no longer' says he is dead. Philip Larkin was an English poet who died in 1985.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was a celebrated poet, a dead maker of verse lines.

clue.text: La Bollard left in hen-house by Teddy

indicators.note: in says the name and the letter go inside the hen-house

parts.note: a roost is where hens sleep
Private Eye's name for the editor Eve Pollard

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor is abandoned in a chicken coop by someone called Teddy.
explanation.walkthrough: La Bollard is Private Eye's mocking name for the newspaper editor Eve Pollard, so it gives EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt was a US president, whose nickname gave the teddy bear its name.

clue.text: Giant boob over article

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this comes first

parts.note: tit is slang for a breast, a boob
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A huge blunder is made about a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' reads as a mistake, but it is the slang for a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth, so the word means any colossus.

clue.text: Capital cover for one about to retire

definitions.text: Capital cover for one about to retire

parts.words: Capital cover for one about to retire
parts.note: capital here means of the head, so this is headwear worn by someone going to bed

explanation.surface: Splendid insurance for a worker on the brink of retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' sounds like money and 'retire' like leaving work; capital is from Latin caput, head, and retiring is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cap traditionally worn in bed, also a drink taken before sleep.

clue.text: Having a problem being popular next to one, Branson, maybe

indicators.note: next to says the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a means one
Branston is a British brand of pickle; the clue twists it into Richard Branson's name

explanation.surface: Richard Branson, beside someone famous, is having trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Branston Pickle is a well-known British chutney; the clue misspells it as the tycoon Branson.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a difficult or awkward situation, a mess.

clue.text: A tight pain in the arse is a real nuisance in public

definitions.text: A tight pain in the arse is a real nuisance in public

parts.words: A tight pain in the arse is a real nuisance in public
parts.note: tight means drunk, so this is a drunken pest making trouble in the street

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' reads as narrow or stingy, but here it is slang for drunk; the answer is the British tabloid word for a beer-fuelled yob.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a young man who drinks beer heavily and behaves rowdily in public places.

clue.text: File put out by Blair finally, a long-term con

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last piece follows
put out means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written before picking its final letter

explanation.surface: Tony Blair releases a dossier that ends up being a lengthy swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle but is short for convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serving a life sentence is a prisoner in for a very long stretch.

clue.text: It's good to go on about things: many a knight's cherished objective

parts.note: to rail is to complain at length

explanation.surface: Grumbling on and on suits medieval knights in pursuit of their dearest goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail was the quest object of Arthurian knights, now any sought-after prize.

clue.text: See 27
Blairzone: cool, Zen-oriented —- there's one inside

parts.note: to fan is to cool

indicators.note: inside says the letter goes within the other letters
oriented means turned round to face a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Blair-themed space, laid back and Zen-like, has someone inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blairzone is pictured as an amateur magazine for devoted fans of Tony Blair.

clue.text: Twins embarrassed about sex — nerds!

indicators.note: about means round, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
embarrassed means discomposed, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: A pair of twins blush on the subject of sex, being geeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe foolish, socially awkward or stupid people, idiots.

clue.text: Scraps banks

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tiers or lines, as a bank of seats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' wants to be leftovers, but it means fights.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means quarrels and also lines of things arranged side by side.

clue.text: Tool pear shaped after starting wank — what a game!

indicators.note: after here says the jumble follows the first letter
starting picks the first letter of the word
shaped means formed into a new arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: A crude tale of a tool going wrong after a solo session, followed by an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pear shaped' reads as one idiom for going wrong, but 'pear' is fodder alongside 'Tool' and 'shaped' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team ball sport played in a swimming pool.

clue.text: Not Maggie's type, comprehensive party wrecker

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher called her moderate Tory opponents wets
blanket means covering everything, comprehensive

explanation.surface: A political party gets ruined by someone Thatcher disliked from a state school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' looks like a British state school, but it means all-inclusive. Wets were the moderate Conservatives Thatcher scorned.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is for a person who dampens everyone's fun at a social gathering.

clue.text: Boycott takes jet to have sex abroad

parts.note: jet black, so jet means black
ball is American slang for have sex

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott flies off on holiday for some foreign romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott is Geoffrey Boycott, the famous Yorkshire cricketer, but it is the verb meaning shun.
explanation.definitionFit: To blackball someone is to vote to exclude them, to shun them.

clue.text: Scandalous rehabilitated lush accepts fame corrupted

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the first jumble holds the second
rehabilitated means reformed, so the letters are made over
corrupted means spoiled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A disgraceful story of a reformed drunk taking in tainted celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct causing disgrace or outrage, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Plenty of cleavage evident from this destroyer of reputations?

definitions.text: Plenty of cleavage evident from this destroyer of reputations?

parts.words: Plenty of cleavage evident from this destroyer of reputations?
parts.note: cleavage here is chopping, done with a small axe, by a person who wrecks reputations

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleavage' suggests a low neckline, but it is the act of cleaving with an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is for someone hired to attack and ruin others' reputations or careers.

clue.text: Warmongering politicians' gobs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: politicians who favour war, belonging to them
second meaning: spits, coughs up phlegm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gobs' looks like mouths, but it is the verb: to gob is to spit, as is to hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names pro-war politicians and is also a verb for clearing the throat and spitting.

clue.text: Complaint: the rest of Europe won't take ours!

definitions.text: the rest of Europe won't take ours!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: British meat, banned by the EU during the 1990s mad cow scare

explanation.walkthrough: The EU banned British beef exports in 1996 over mad cow disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a grievance and is also the cattle meat Europe refused to import.

clue.text: Shrink wrap rook in bad blood

indicators.note: wrap with in instructs putting one thing inside another
in, after wrap, says where the chess piece goes

parts.note: a feud is lasting bad blood between parties
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Shrink wrap a chess piece in a bitter quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink wrap' reads as packaging film; 'Shrink' is the definition, slang for psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis, the archetypal psychiatrist, called a shrink in slang.

clue.text: Spice girl after head

indicators.note: after says the girl comes after the head

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl chasing someone at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice girl' suggests the pop group, but 'Spice' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a kitchen spice.

clue.text: Hand job bloke

parts.note: work means a job
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A smutty phrase for a sex act performed by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a rude phrase, but 'Hand' is the definition, as in a farm hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual labourer, as in factory hand or farm hand.

clue.text: In Bavaria, Bundestag upset an old part of Egypt

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the hidden letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters IABUN sit inside these words, across the end of Bavaria and the start of Bundestag

explanation.surface: A German parliamentary crisis in Bavaria somehow involves ancient Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters across the end of Bavaria and start of Bundestag, IABUN, read backwards gives NUBAI, not the answer, so 'upset' must be taken as rearranging them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an ancient region along the Nile, partly in southern Egypt.

clue.text: This sort of sandwich a big hit

definitions.text: This sort of sandwich a big hit

parts.words: This sort of sandwich a big hit
parts.note: a slang sandwich that is really a punch in the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'A big hit' sounds like a popular success, but it is a punch; the slang sandwich is a fist in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means a punch, the hand's joint being the filling delivered to the mouth.

clue.text: Bad lad Kelvin on church body!

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed on top, so this comes first

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin temperature unit
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A naughty boy called Kelvin sits on the church council.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest rogue, a villainous man.

clue.text: Swindle southern softie

parts.note: poof is old offensive British slang for an effeminate man, here a softie

explanation.surface: A con trick played by a soft southerner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a hoax or trick, a deception.

clue.text: A couple of blokes who can no longer score getting pissed

definitions.text: A couple of blokes who can no longer score
definitions.meaning: first meaning: two dead composers who will write no more scores
second meaning: rhyming slang for drunk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests sex or goals, but it means writing music. Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dead composers, and the pair's names rhyme with the slang word for drunk.

clue.text: "No Ecstasy left? Everyone's into crack plus a bit of heroin!", as this star might say?

indicators.note: plus says the next piece is added on the end

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: into says the group goes inside the joke

parts.note: a crack is a joke, a gag
everyone is all
the first three letters of the word heroin

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled cry about running out of pills, taking crack and heroin, the kind of thing a rock star might say.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1997 the Oasis songwriter caused a stir by saying taking drugs was like having a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: He was Oasis's guitarist and songwriter, a Britpop star known for remarks about drugs.
